events.title: Eastern Market — Weekend Market & Flea
events.description: Historic public market plus weekend outdoor flea, arts, and crafts. Live music when weather permits.

events.title: Capitol Hill Farmers Markets
events.description: Seasonal weekend farmers markets with local produce and vendors.

events.title: Lincoln Park
events.description: Large Capitol Hill green space with playground, paths, and statues. Dog-friendly. Cafes at both ends.

events.title: Garfield Park
events.description: Neighborhood park with playground, tennis, basketball, bocce, and a community garden.

events.title: Yards Park & Navy Yard Waterfront
events.description: Riverfront park with fountains, boardwalk, and frequent seasonal weekend programming.

events.title: National Mall & Smithsonian Museums
events.description: Free Smithsonian museums and monuments. Reliable all-weather, all-ages option.

events.title: United States Botanic Garden
events.description: Free conservatory and gardens at the foot of the Capitol, with a Children's Garden.

events.title: Anacostia Riverwalk Trail Ride
events.description: Paved riverfront trail for a family bike ride, with Capital Bikeshare access nearby.

events.title: The Fields at RFK — Community Open Play & Disc Golf
events.time: Open hours vary (8 AM–dusk disc golf)
events.venue: The Fields at RFK Campus (401 Oklahoma Ave NE)
events.description: Turf fields with community open-play hours plus DC's free disc golf course. 10-min walk from Stadium-Armory.

events.title: CHAW Gallery (Capitol Hill Arts Workshop)
events.venue: Capitol Hill Arts Workshop (545 7th St SE)
events.description: Rotating gallery shows of local artists, two blocks from Eastern Market. Check site for current exhibition.

events.title: Kennedy Center Outdoor Film Series
events.description: Free outdoor film screenings on the Kennedy Center REACH campus video wall, held most Friday evenings through late August. Last showing August 29.

events.title: Sam Salem
events.description: National touring stand-up comedian Sam Salem headlines the DC Comedy Loft for a weekend run, August 27–29. The Comedy Loft is an intimate club in Dupont Circle seating around 200, with every table close to the stage.

events.title: DC Summer Restaurant Week
events.description: Metropolitan Washington Summer Restaurant Week returns August 24–30 with special prix-fixe pricing at more than 150 restaurants across the city.

events.title: DC250 Market / National Farmers' Market Week on the Mall
events.venue: National Mall, between Constitution & Independence Ave SW
events.description: Over 80 vendors from across the country celebrate National Farmers' Market Week along the National Mall, with live music, live art, DC culture showcases, and family-friendly activities as part of the DC250 Market.

events.title: DC Festival of Magic
events.description: Back for a sixth year at the Capital Hilton, the DC Festival of Magic brings together the best magicians in the Mid-Atlantic region for three nights of Labor Day weekend entertainment. All-access passes cover five shows total.

events.title: DC JazzFest — Full Festival Run (City-Wide)
events.description: The 22nd annual DC JazzFest runs September 2–6 across the city, celebrating jazz with the theme 'The Future of Jazz: America's Next 250 Years.' Features NEA Jazz Masters, GRAMMY winners, emerging stars, and international artists at venues city-wide, with free Meet the Artist programs at Arena Stage.

events.title: DC JazzFest at The Wharf
events.venue: The Wharf — District Pier, Arena Stage, Union Stage, Pearl Street Warehouse
events.description: The grand finale of DC JazzFest 2026 — a two-day waterfront celebration on District Pier featuring NEA Jazz Masters, GRAMMY winners, and global artists including Dee Dee Bridgewater, Kurt Elling, Bill Frisell, Cory Henry & The Funk Apostles, and Emmet Cohen. Theme: 'The Future of Jazz: America's Next 250 Years.' Additional indoor shows at Arena Stage, Union Stage, and Pearl Street Warehouse.

events.title: DC JazzFest at The Wharf – 22nd Annual Grand Finale Weekend
events.venue: District Pier & Transit Pier – The Wharf (+ Arena Stage, Union Stage, Pearl Street Warehouse)
events.description: The two-day grand finale of the 22nd annual DC Jazz Festival takes place on District Pier and Transit Pier at The Wharf over Labor Day weekend, featuring NEA Jazz Masters, Grammy winners, and international artists including Dee Dee Bridgewater, Joshua Redman, Cory Henry & The Funk Apostles, Nate Smith, Samara Joy, and more. Additional indoor performances at Arena Stage, Union Stage, and Pearl Street Warehouse. Family-friendly with a kids' scavenger hunt for ages under 15. Tickets start at $25.

events.title: Marcus D. Wiley
events.description: Marcus D. Wiley headlines DC Improv with multiple upcoming shows confirmed at the venue (1140 Connecticut Ave NW). DC Improv requires patrons to be 18 or older and enforces a 2-item food/beverage minimum.

events.title: Art All Night 2026 – Eastern Market & Barracks Row Activation
events.venue: Eastern Market & Barracks Row (8th Street SE)
events.description: Eastern Market and Barracks Row host activations as part of Art All Night 2026, the city-wide public arts festival themed 'The Art of Music.' The Eastern Market/Barracks Row programming runs Friday September 11 through Saturday September 12.

events.title: Art All Night DC
events.description: DC's all-night arts festival spreading across several neighborhoods, showcasing painting, performing arts, music, and sculpture in both public and private spaces, indoors and outdoors. Companion event Dine All Night runs concurrently.

events.title: Eastern Market Weekend – Outdoor Farmers & Arts Market
events.description: Eastern Market's historic open-air weekend programming continues every Saturday and Sunday through the fall, featuring local farmers, artisans, and handmade arts and crafts vendors. A Capitol Hill community staple for 152 years.

events.title: Wharf Saturday Farmers Market at M Street Landing
events.description: The Wharf's weekly Saturday farmers market at M Street Landing features locally sourced food and produce from regional farmers, running through the fall season.

events.title: DC Public Library – 'District Vibes / American Pride' Exhibition
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library
events.description: On view through all three target weekends, this public art exhibition at the MLK Library explores how DC changed American culture. Part of the DC Public Library's Public Arts & Exhibits program. Accessible during all target weekends (Aug 29–30, Sep 5–6, Sep 12–13). No registration required.

events.title: Sunset Cinema at The Wharf
events.description: Free outdoor waterfront movie screenings on Transit Pier at The Wharf, presented by Pacifico Beer, with views of the Potomac. Runs through September 30, 2026.

events.title: Dirty Dancing
events.description: The classic story of Baby and Johnny comes to life in this Broadway touring production of Dirty Dancing, playing a limited engagement at DC's National Theatre on Pennsylvania Avenue.

events.title: Venus
events.price: Tickets available; Woolly offers Pay-What-You-Can performances and $20 under-30 pricing
events.description: A darkly comic play by Steve Yockey, directed by new Woolly Mammoth Artistic Director Reggie D. White. Nicole and Beth are opposites who attract until a midnight date under the stars pushes their romance to the brink, with a mysterious woman in a red raincoat emerging as their antagonist.

events.title: WIT Escape with Washington Improv Theater
events.description: WIT's 'Escape with Washington Improv Theater' series runs through the fall at Studio Theatre (1501 14th St. NW) — first four weeks in the Milton theater, then the Shargai space. Featuring WIT's funniest ensemble improvisers in totally unscripted, audience-suggested longform improv. No two shows are alike.

events.title: The Great Privation (How to flip ten cents into a dollar)
events.price: Tickets available; Woolly offers Pay-What-You-Can performances and $20 under-30 pricing
events.description: A world premiere, time-bending new play by Nia Akilah Robinson, co-produced by Woolly Mammoth and Boston's Company One Theatre. An evocative exploration running through early October.

events.title: Measure for Measure
events.price: Season subscriptions from $156; single tickets TBA; special rates for under-35, students, seniors, military
events.description: Shakespeare's rarely staged comedy — last seen at Folger in 2006 — directed by Psalmayene 24 (Helen Hayes Award winner). Where human nature collides with the letter of the law: a corrupt official tries to coerce a novice nun as Vienna's citizens navigate newly enforced regulations. Opens the Folger Theatre 2026–27 season.

events.title: Merrily We Roll Along
events.description: Stephen Sondheim and George Furth's beloved musical staged by Signature Theatre in Arlington. The audience follows a trio of close friends across 20 years in reverse chronological order — from their lowest moment to their highest — marked by incredible Sondheim songs. A rumination on friendship, compromise, and the cost of success.

events.title: The Fruits of Our Labor
events.price: Tickets from ~$45; under-30 / rush discounts available
events.description: A world-premiere dance-theater event from Step Afrika! commemorating America's 250th anniversary. Directed by Jakari Sherman, the production blends stepping, percussion, poetry, and song into a rhythmic exploration of American history and identity.

events.title: Nikola – A New Musical
events.price: Tickets from ~$45; under-30 / rush discounts available
events.description: A world-premiere musical charting the rise of inventor Nikola Tesla from unknown engineer to eccentric genius. Book and lyrics by Nikko Benson and Benjamin Halstead, music by Nikko Benson, directed by Marshall Pailet. As his rivalry with Thomas Edison intensifies, Tesla pushes himself and the limits of electric power to dangerous extremes.

events.title: National Geographic Museum of Exploration
events.venue: National Geographic Society HQ, 1600 M St NW
events.description: The brand-new 100,000-square-foot National Geographic Museum of Exploration, open at the organization's historic DC campus through end of year.

events.title: USBG Ongoing Exhibits: Fierce Flora & America's State Flowers
events.description: Two concurrent free exhibits at the US Botanic Garden available all three target weekends. 'Fierce Flora: Tales of Survival and Demise' highlights the unique survival features plants have evolved to defend themselves — carnivorous plants, toxic species, and more. 'America's State Flowers: An America250 Celebration' is a garden-wide display of flowers representing all U.S. states and territories. No tickets required.

events.title: Hill Family Biking: Back-to-School Ride & Block Party
events.venue: School Within School (920 F St. NE)
events.description: A 4-mile progressive bike ride touring many Capitol Hill schools — Ludlow-Taylor, J.O. Wilson, Capitol Hill Montessori, Stuart-Hobson, Peabody, Maury, and Miner — with families able to join at different points along the route. Afterward, a block party with foam party, DJ, giant chalk art, face painting, balance bike course, and food truck. MPD bike team will also participate. Bike maintenance help available 15 minutes before ride start.

events.title: Jenny Tian
events.description: Australian-Chinese comedian Jenny Tian returns to DC Improv in 2026 with a brand new hour after selling out her 2025 debut. Named by Deadline as a stand-up to watch in 2026, she has toured Edinburgh Fringe, the West End, and across the US.

events.title: Pump Action
events.description: Live music at Pearl Street Warehouse. All shows at this venue are 21+ unless otherwise noted.
events.source: opendate.io (Pearl Street Warehouse official booking platform)

events.title: Smithsonian Free Museum Weekends – August 29–30
events.description: All 17 Smithsonian DC-area museums offer free admission every day, including weekends. Highlights for late August include the National Museum of American History's 'In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness' (America 250 flagship exhibition), the National Air and Space Museum's interactive flight galleries, the National Museum of Natural History, the National Zoo, and the Smithsonian American Art Museum. Touchless scavenger hunts available at select locations.

events.title: Pints for Paws with Pacifico
events.description: A tail-wagging afternoon by the water benefiting Lucky Dog Animal Rescue, presented by Pacifico Beer on Transit Pier at The Wharf.

events.title: Pints for Paws with Pacifico – Waterfront Dog Rescue Benefit
events.description: A tail-wagging afternoon by the water at The Wharf benefiting Lucky Dog Animal Rescue, presented by Pacifico Beer.

events.title: Perfekt Blend Free Concert at The Wharf
events.venue: The Wharf — Floating Stage, Transit Pier
events.description: Genre-defying high entertainment group Perfekt Blend performs on the Floating Stage at Transit Pier. Free concert presented by Pacifico Beer.

events.title: Rock the Dock: Perfekt Blend (R&B) – Free Pier Concert
events.venue: Transit Pier, Floating Stage – The Wharf
events.description: Genre-defying high entertainment group Perfekt Blend performs on the Floating Stage at Transit Pier as the final installment of the Rock the Dock free summer concert series, presented by Pacifico Beer.

events.title: Ken Carson with Xaviersobased, Prettifun, and DJ Moon
events.description: Hip-hop/rap show at The Anthem featuring Ken Carson with supporting acts Xaviersobased, Prettifun, and DJ Moon.

events.title: RFK Legacy: A Tailgate Experience – Free Community Celebration
events.description: Events DC hosts a free community celebration honoring the history of RFK Memorial Stadium, featuring food, live performances, fan experiences, autograph and photo opportunities with DC baseball and football legends, intramural sports, and family-friendly activities.

events.title: Smithsonian Free Museum Weekends – September 5–6
events.description: All 17 Smithsonian DC-area museums are free every weekend. The Renwick Gallery's current exhibition closes September 7, making this one of the last weekends to catch it. The National Museum of American History's America 250 flagship exhibition 'In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness' remains on view. Smithsonian Castle partial first-floor access is also open through September 7.

events.title: WABA Adult Trail Riding Basics – DC
events.venue: Anacostia Boat Ramp Parking Lot, Anacostia Park
events.price: Paid (registration required; check waba.org for pricing)
events.description: A WABA skills class for adults who already know how to ride a bike but want more confidence on trails, or who recently completed a Learn to Ride or Basic Skills class. Participants must bring their own bike and helmet in good working order. Capital Bikeshare bikes are reimbursable for the class duration — email education@waba.org for details.

events.title: DC State Fair
events.venue: Brookland neighborhood (exact location TBD — check dcstatefair.org)
events.description: A free daylong showcase of the District's agricultural, culinary, and creative talents inspired by time-honored state fair traditions. Activities include competitions for best photographer, best mumbo sauce, micro-garden contests, slime for kids, and more.

events.title: NSO Labor Day Concert on the Capitol Lawn
events.venue: West Lawn of the U.S. Capitol
events.description: The National Symphony Orchestra's free annual Labor Day weekend concert returns to the West Lawn of the U.S. Capitol. No tickets required; seating is first-come, first-served.

events.title: Peter Hook and The Light
events.description: Rock show from Peter Hook and The Light. The 9:30 Club is general admission and all ages unless otherwise stated.

events.title: Becky Robinson – The Beasts in Me Tour
events.description: Becky Robinson brings The Beasts in Me Tour to the historic Lincoln Theatre on U Street.

events.title: Capitol Riverfront Friday Night Concert Series – Yards Park (Final Weekend)
events.description: The 14th season of the Capitol Riverfront's free Friday Night Concert Series at the Yards Park boardwalk stage. Family-friendly outdoor concert with river views, food and drink available nearby. September 11 is the final Friday of the season. Specific artist TBD – check capitolriverfront.org for confirmed lineup.

events.title: 10th Annual DC Bike Ride
events.venue: Start: 12th St NW & Constitution Ave NW; Finish: Pennsylvania Ave NW & 7th St NW
events.price: Paid registration (youth 8–17 half price; kids 3–7 free with adult; standard ~$59+)
events.description: The 10th Annual DC Bike Ride takes participants on a scenic 20-mile car-free route through city streets, past monuments and memorials, and across the Potomac River. Welcomes riders age 3 and up. The free Finish Festival on Pennsylvania Ave features live music, food trucks, and a beer garden — open to the public.

events.title: 2026 DC Bike Ride
events.time: 6:00 AM corrals open; 8:00 AM ride begins; 8:30 AM Finish Festival
events.venue: 12th St. NW & Constitution Ave. NW (Start Line)
events.price: Paid; Youth (ages 8–17) half-price; Kids 3–7 free with paying adult; College discounts available
events.description: DC's signature annual car-free cycling event gathering thousands of riders for a flat, scenic 20-mile course through iconic landmarks and across the Potomac River into Virginia and back. All levels and ages 3+ welcome — a celebration, not a race. Live music, rest stops with food and drinks, and an epic Finish Festival near the Capitol Building with food trucks, beer garden, and live entertainment. Bike rentals available.

events.title: Damon Wayans Jr.
events.description: Damon Wayans Jr. is listed as an upcoming headliner at The Comedy Loft of DC (1523 22nd St NW, Dupont Circle). The intimate club hosts national headliners with seating for around 200 and a 2-item minimum.

events.title: Female Athlete Recognition Day at The Wharf
events.description: A free, family-friendly day at The Wharf celebrating and recognizing today's female athletes.

events.title: Smithsonian Free Museum Weekends – September 12–13
events.description: All 17 Smithsonian DC-area museums are free every weekend. September 12–13 is also the weekend preceding Smithsonian Magazine's Annual Museum Day (Sept 13/17 depending on source — see separate listing), making it an ideal time to explore both Smithsonian and participating non-Smithsonian institutions. Natural History Museum's Q?rius science education center hosts drop-in programming for teens.

events.title: Venjent
events.description: British electronic music producer and performer Venjent plays the 9:30 Club.

events.title: Willow Avalon
events.description: Country and Americana singer-songwriter Willow Avalon performs at 9:30 Club.

events.title: Women in Sports Day at The Wharf – Free Family Event
events.description: A free, family-friendly day at The Wharf celebrating today's female athletes. Programming details TBD — check wharfdc.com/upcoming-events for the full schedule.

events.title: Adams Morgan Day Festival
events.description: The longest-running neighborhood festival in the District — over 40 years old. The lively 18th Street buzzes with music, food vendors, for-sale artwork, and family-friendly activities celebrating one of DC's most diverse neighborhoods.

events.title: Pints for Paws at The Wharf (September edition)
events.description: Pints for Paws with Pacifico returns to The Wharf for an afternoon by the water benefiting a local animal rescue organization.

events.title: Smithsonian Magazine Annual Museum Day
events.price: Free (free ticket required from Smithsonian Magazine)
events.description: Smithsonian Magazine's Annual Museum Day opens hundreds of cultural institutions across the country for free to anyone with a downloadable Museum Day ticket. In DC, participating institutions typically include museums that normally charge admission. Download a free ticket at smithsonianmag.com before the event. Over 100,000 tickets are expected to be given away nationally.

events.title: WABA Adult Learn to Ride – Arlington (VA)
events.venue: Quincy St. Parking Deck, Arlington, VA (directions sent in confirmation email)
events.price: Paid (check waba.org for current pricing; sponsored by BikeArlington)
events.description: WABA's 3-hour Adult Learn to Ride class for participants 18 and older who have never ridden a bike or want to build foundational skills. Experienced instructors work step-by-step on starting, stopping, balancing, gliding, pedaling, and steering at a 1:5 instructor-to-participant ratio. Group class of up to 25 participants. Participants can have a bike reserved by providing height at registration.

events.title: USBG Summer Evening Hours with Live Music – September Edition
events.description: The final Summer Evening Hours of 2026 at the USBG — the Garden stays open until 8 PM for golden hour and sunset. Live music by Josee Molavi, performing soul-jazz with alternative R&B and pop influences. The 'America's State Flowers: An America250 Celebration' garden-wide exhibit remains on view. Vintage Views offers lemonade, botanical mocktails, and snacks for purchase. No tickets required.

events.title: Library of Congress Family Day: Celebrating 50 Years of the American Folklife Center
events.description: A drop-in family day at the Library of Congress celebrating the 50th anniversary of the American Folklife Center. Includes creative activities, displays, and conversations with Library staff experts. Each Family Day features hands-on projects, connections to Library of Congress collections, and ways to use Library resources at home. Free passes required for entry to the Jefferson Building.

events.title: The Best of Steve Martin & Martin Short
events.description: Comedy icons Steve Martin and Martin Short bring their celebrated collaborative show to DAR Constitution Hall on September 19, 2026. Their show interweaves anecdotes about their Hollywood careers, musical interludes, and playful banter — a nostalgic yet fresh evening for all ages.

events.title: Militarie Gun
events.description: Militarie Gun live at Black Cat on U Street.

events.title: Colin Armstrong
events.description: Rising stand-up Colin Armstrong headlines DC Comedy Loft. His viral comedy videos have amassed tens of millions of views; he's been featured on SiriusXM and performed alongside John Mulaney and Marc Maron at the 2026 Lil' Rhody Laugh Riot Comedy Festival.

events.title: Ryan Beatty
events.description: Ryan Beatty performs at the Lincoln Theatre. Tickets start from $83.

events.title: Erica Rhodes: Call Me Crazy Tour
events.description: Erica Rhodes — one of Deadline Hollywood's Comics to Watch for 2026 and a breakout from America's Got Talent — brings her CALL ME CRAZY tour to the Arlington Cinema & Drafthouse. Her comedy has been featured on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, Just For Laughs, and Netflix Is a Joke Fest.

events.title: Improv for All! Workshop at MLK Library (September)
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library
events.description: DC Public Library partners with Washington Improv Theater (WIT) for a free, beginner-friendly 90-minute improv workshop. High-fun, low-stress — no theater experience or comedy background needed. Offered monthly at MLK Library; the confirmed September date is Sept 27 (just outside the target weekends but the closest confirmed instance). Registration required and tends to fill up. Check dclibrary.libnet.info for August and earlier September dates as they are posted.

events.title: Lucinda Williams
events.description: Legendary singer-songwriter Lucinda Williams performs at the Lincoln Theatre. Also listed at 9:30 Club on Songkick — Lincoln Theatre confirmed via SeatGeek with explicit ticket price.

events.title: Bear Ghost, Sarah & the Safe Word, and Spaceman Bob
events.description: Multi-act show at Black Cat featuring Bear Ghost headlining with Sarah & the Safe Word and Spaceman Bob.

events.title: Buffalo Traffic Jam
events.description: Buffalo Traffic Jam live at the 9:30 Club.

events.title: Wave To Earth
events.description: South Korean indie band Wave To Earth performs at The Anthem.

events.title: Damien Lemon
events.description: Comedian, writer, and actor Damien Lemon headlines Arlington Cinema & Drafthouse. Host of TruTV's Comedy Knockout and a long-time cast member/writer for MTV2's Guy Code and Hip-Hop Squares; also seen on Comedy Central's The Half-Hour, Broad City, HBO's Crashing, and The Night Of.

events.title: Found Footage Fest: Porcelain VHS Treasures
events.description: Brand new show for 2026 at Arlington Drafthouse: Found Footage Fest — live comedy performed with actual VHS tapes. A unique, riff-style live show in the beloved Found Footage Fest tradition.

events.title: Frog
events.description: Frog performs at Black Cat. (Likely a separate event from Woods on the same date — Black Cat has multiple stages.)

events.title: Knocked Loose and Denzel Curry with Superheaven and Boundaries
events.description: Massive double-headliner show: Knocked Loose (hardcore) and Denzel Curry (hip-hop) co-headline The Anthem, with Superheaven and Boundaries supporting.

events.title: The California Honeydrops
events.description: Soul and R&B outfit The California Honeydrops perform at the 9:30 Club.

events.title: Woods
events.description: Indie/folk-rock band Woods performs at Black Cat.

events.title: Ceremony, Poison Ruïn, and Dry Socket
events.description: Punk/hardcore triple-bill featuring Ceremony, Poison Ruïn, and Dry Socket at Black Cat.

events.title: Indigo Girls and Linda Perry
events.description: Iconic folk-rock duo Indigo Girls perform at The Anthem with Linda Perry.

events.title: Medium Build and Ken Yates
events.description: Medium Build headlines with Ken Yates supporting at the 9:30 Club.
